[[File:Bifurcations and crises of Ikeda attractor.png|thumb|Bifurcations and crises in the [[Ikeda map]].]]

In [[applied mathematics]] and [[astrodynamics]], in the theory of [[dynamical systems]], a '''crisis''' is the sudden appearance or disappearance of a [[strange attractor]] as the parameters of a [[dynamical system]] are varied.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Grebogi | first1=Celso | last2=Ott | first2=Edward | last3=Yorke | first3=James A. | title=Crises, sudden changes in chaotic attractors, and transient chaos | journal=Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=7 | issue=1–3 | year=1983 | issn=0167-2789 | doi=10.1016/0167-2789(83)90126-4 | pages=181–200| bibcode=1983PhyD....7..181G }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Nayfeh | first1=Ali H. | last2=Balachandran | first2=Balakumar | title=Applied Nonlinear Dynamics: Analytical, Computational, and Experimental Methods | publisher=Wiley | date=1995-03-29 | isbn=978-0-471-59348-5 | doi=10.1002/9783527617548 }}</ref> This [[Bifurcation theory#Global bifurcations|global bifurcation]] occurs when a [[Chaos theory|chaotic]] attractor comes into contact with an [[unstable]] [[periodic orbit]] or its [[stable manifold]].<ref>[[Vladimir Arnold|Arnol’d, V.I.]], Afraimovich, V.S., Ilyashenko, Yu.S. & Shilnikov, L.P. 1993. Bifurcation theory and catastrophe theory. In Dynamical Systems, vol. 5, Berlin and New York: Springer</ref> As the orbit approaches the unstable orbit it will diverge away from the previous attractor, leading to a qualitatively different behaviour. Crises can produce [[intermittency|intermittent]] behaviour.

Grebogi, Ott, Romeiras, and Yorke distinguished between three types of crises:<ref>{{cite journal | last1=GREBOGI | first1=C. | last2=OTT | first2=E. | last3=YORKE | first3=J. A. | title=Chaos, Strange Attractors, and Fractal Basin Boundaries in Nonlinear Dynamics | journal=Science | publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) | volume=238 | issue=4827 | date=1987-10-30 | issn=0036-8075 | doi=10.1126/science.238.4827.632 | pages=632–638| pmid=17816542 | bibcode=1987Sci...238..632G | s2cid=1586349 }}</ref>

* The first type, a '''boundary''' or an '''exterior crisis''', the attractor is suddenly destroyed as the parameters are varied. In the postbifurcation state the motion is transiently chaotic, moving chaotically along the former attractor before being attracted to a [[Fixed point (mathematics)|fixed point]], periodic orbit, [[Quasiperiodic motion|quasiperiodic orbit]], another strange attractor, or diverging to infinity.
* In the second type of crisis, an '''interior crisis''', the size of the chaotic attractor suddenly increases. The attractor encounters an unstable fixed point or periodic solution that is inside the [[basin of attraction]].
* In the third type, an '''attractor merging crisis''', two or more chaotic attractors merge to form a single attractor as the critical parameter value is passed.

Note that the reverse case (sudden appearance, shrinking or splitting of attractors) can also occur. The latter two crises are sometimes called explosive bifurcations.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Thompson | first1=J. M. T. | last2=Stewart | first2=H. B. | last3=Ueda | first3=Y. | title=Safe, explosive, and dangerous bifurcations in dissipative dynamical systems | journal=Physical Review E | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=49 | issue=2 | date=1994-02-01 | issn=1063-651X | doi=10.1103/physreve.49.1019 | pages=1019–1027| pmid=9961309 | bibcode=1994PhRvE..49.1019T }}</ref>

While crises are "sudden" as a parameter is varied, the dynamics of the system over time can show long transients before orbits leave the neighbourhood of the old attractor. Typically there is a time constant τ for the length of the transient that diverges as a power law (τ&nbsp;≈&nbsp;|''p''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;''p''<sub>c</sub>|<sup>''γ''</sup>) near the critical parameter value ''p''<sub>c</sub>. The exponent ''γ'' is called the critical crisis exponent.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Grebogi | first1=Celso | last2=Ott | first2=Edward | last3=Romeiras | first3=Filipe | last4=Yorke | first4=James A. | title=Critical exponents for crisis-induced intermittency | journal=Physical Review A | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=36 | issue=11 | date=1987-12-01 | issn=0556-2791 | doi=10.1103/physreva.36.5365 | pages=5365–5380| pmid=9898807 | bibcode=1987PhRvA..36.5365G }}</ref> There also exist systems where the divergence is stronger than a power law, so-called super-persistent chaotic transients.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Grebogi | first1=Celso | last2=Ott | first2=Edward | last3=Yorke | first3=James A. | title=Super persistent chaotic transients | journal=Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems | publisher=Cambridge University Press (CUP) | volume=5 | issue=3 | year=1985 | issn=0143-3857 | doi=10.1017/s014338570000300x | pages=341–372| doi-access=free }}</ref>
